Explaining how drops works in the web platform (not only editor) is something worth mentioning both in [Web Editor Documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/using_the_web_editor.html#limitations) and [DisplayServer.window_set_drop_files_callback()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_displayserver.html#class-displayserver-method-window-set-drop-files-callback). Particularly that user should not rely on persistence of such files since they are deleted right after the drop callback finishes, so they should copy or move them to a new location.

They will be both rejected by the condition in the outer block below with `"Importing multiple ZIP projects is not supported."`

Emscripten provides a [virtual file system](https://emscripten.org/docs/api_reference/Filesystem-API.html) abstraction similar to the POSIX API.

The default "driver" (where `/` is mounted from) is an in-memory file system ([MEMFS](https://emscripten.org/docs/api_reference/Filesystem-API.html#filesystem-api-memfs)), and we specifically mount `/userfs` (and `/home/web_user` in editor) using the [IDBFS](https://emscripten.org/docs/api_reference/Filesystem-API.html#filesystem-api-idbfs) driver (which uses the [IndexedDB](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IndexedDB_API) to persist).

For this reason, when the application is shutdown and the memory is freed the contents outside those persistent folders is lost.

As per the PR description, the signal parameter (`p_files`) only contains the top level items.

So if `p_files` contains a ZIP, that ZIP is not inside a folder, and thus not part of a project.

I've done some renaming, the big `DROP` is now `ROOT` (since it's the root folder where the drop happens).

The "controller" is now called `drop`, so you `process(drop, ...)`, and the function is called `create_drop`.

The `drops` variable passed to the callback is now just `out`.
